summary:
## Idea
An int32-backed fixed representation with 16 fractional bits. Integer-facing arithmetic uses explicit rounding and saturation; multiply avoids an int64 hot path.

## Complexity
Arithmetic operations have fixed-width bounded work; integer square root uses a bounded iteration. Storage O(1).

## Use when
A reproducible integer-backed numeric contract with documented saturation fits the domain.

## Avoid when
The dynamic range or precision needs exceed Q16.16, or silent saturation would hide an invalid model.

## Pitfalls
Read each operation's rounding and division edge rules. ofFloat/toFloat are only Portable in the profile; the record grade covers the integer-facing core.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Algorithms; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Algorithms.Numerics.Fixed.ofRatio: int -> int -> Fixed`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Algorithms.Numerics
let threeHalves = Fixed.ofRatio 3 2
let square = Fixed.mul threeHalves threeHalves
let whole = Fixed.toIntFloor square
```

## Tests
FixedTests: exact BigInteger oracles, a fixed-seed 100000-pair sweep and ADR0098 edge vectors.

## Bench
The cited archived 0.2.0 baseline contains numerics/fixed-q16-16/mul-div-sqrt. Read its source commit, host/date/toolchain, sizes, work counts, runtime-specific median/p95 and spread. These are GitHub-hosted runner-class comparisons, not quiet-host absolute performance; this later source revision is not itself remeasured.
